messages.subject: Handling irregular Time Series
messages.body_plain:
Dear INLA community,

I am fitting a spatio-temporal model for Italian voter turnout using a Beta likelihood (family = "beta") on an areal dataset covering (N = 107) provinces over (T = 10) national parliamentary elections between 1987 and 2022.

Because elections do not occur on a regular schedule, the time intervals between consecutive elections vary between 2 and 5 years.

I was modelling it with something like:

  formula <- Y ~ 1 + Covariates + f(Time_Cont, model = "ou", values = target_time_cont, hyper = pc_prior_ou) + f(id_space, model = "bym2", graph = g_prov, scale.model = TRUE, hyper = pc_prior_bym2) + f(id_space_int, model = "besag", graph = g_prov, group = id_time_discrete, control.group = list(model = "ar1", hyper = pc_prior_ar1))

which brought me good results in model fit and residual analysis, but I am not completely sure about the validity of such an approach.

I was wondering whether the best way to handle irregular time series is:

1. treating discrete election steps as equidistant using AR(1), as in the above formula

2. trying data augmentation

3. other possibilities...

Thank you in advance for your Help,

Kind regards,

Max

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Handling irregular Time Series
messages.body_plain:
you can use a finer resolution for your AR1, like having the AR1 on every year,
and then you just observe the elections when you have them. the easy way to do
this is to add the argument 'values', which defines where the AR1 is defined

with only AR1, then we get

y ~ f(year, model="ar1", values = 1:10)

then with

y <- c(10, 20)
year <- c(2, 5)

we observe 10 at year 2, 20 at year 5. the AR1 is defined every year

this is the easiest way out.

of course you can use a finer scale as well.
